en: The northeast monsoon (amihan) brings cool, dry air to the Philippines between November and February.
Mayon Volcano's frequent eruptions enrich the surrounding soil with ash, making it highly fertile for farming abaca.
Pumice is a light, porous volcanic rock that can actually float on water when first ejected.
Baguio City often experiences thick fog because warm, moist air cools and condenses at high elevations.
The Sun provides the energy that drives the water cycle by evaporating water from the West Philippine Sea.
The bright star Sirius, part of the Orion constellation, is the most luminous star visible in the Philippine night sky.
The gravitational pull of the Moon causes the daily rising and falling of ocean tides in Manila Bay.
A storm surge is an abnormal rise in seawater pushed ashore by strong typhoon winds, unlike a tsunami.
A rainbow forms when sunlight refracts and reflects inside spherical raindrops after a brief afternoon thunderstorm.
The white sand beaches of Boracay are primarily composed of eroded quartz minerals and crushed coral fragments.
During an El Niño event, the Philippines experiences below-average rainfall, leading to severe droughts and water shortages.
Heavy rains can remobilize loose volcanic ash from Mount Pinatubo into fast-flowing, destructive mudflows called lahars.
